wins.claim: KerfDesk's operationOverride forks the full per-layer settings block per object with compiler-verified preview/G-code/estimate consistency, vs LightBurn's power-scale-only Shape Properties.
KerfDesk layers carry full cut settings with LightBurn's Show/Output semantics; xTool Studio's stroke-color layers hold no parameters and only speed multi-select.
KerfDesk's per-layer set (kerf, tabs, hatch controls, 11 dithers, air, per-device defaults) far exceeds xTool Studio's documented power/speed/passes triad.

gaps.claim: No Z offset/Z-step per pass, perforation, dot mode, cut-through delays, or ramp; image overscan hard-coded at 5 mm; none of these absences ADR-recorded.
Sub-layers work but the dialog silently discards a dead 'Visible' checkbox, sub-layers cannot be drag-reordered, and the divergence has no ADR.
No .clb import, no linked presets, no manufacturer/community library; starter content covers one machine (7 presets) vs XCS's official multi-machine EasySet (−2 vs XCS).
Reordering is single-step up/down only — no drag-and-drop, no move-to-top/bottom, and no auto-sort like 'Sort Cuts Last' or XCS's Auto Planning (−2 vs XCS).
Silent clamps, layer-card redirect on selection, Delete removes artwork against WORKFLOW F-A7, Material Library default-collapsed, no drag reorder, no settings copy/paste.
No fixed palette strip; assignment is a free color picker plus per-row Assign button rather than LightBurn's one-click palette assignment.
